faq.a: Shirin is associated with the Persian form شِيرِين, whose core sense is shirin; sweet (persian).

faq.q: What is the origin of Shirin?
faq.a: Shirin is associated with Persian. Shirin is Persian شیرین (shīrīn), meaning 'sweet'. It is used as a female given name in Iran, Central Asia and South Asia.
No — the underlying form is Persian, not Arabic.
Shirin can occur in Muslim naming contexts, but it is better described as a Persian-origin name used within some Muslim naming traditions than as an exclusively Islamic religious term.
Shirin should not be classified as a Quranic personal name without a direct Quranic basis. Shīrīn is a Persian word, not a Quranic Arabic form.

faq.q: What does Shirin mean in Urdu?
faq.a: In Urdu, Shirin is rendered شیریں and carries the sense شیریں، میٹھی.

faq.q: What does Shirin mean in Persian?
faq.a: In Persian, Shirin is rendered شیرین and carries the sense شیرین، شیرین.
A romanized syllable approximation is shi-rin. No IPA transcription is asserted because a verified phonetic transcription was not available.

faq.q: What are the variants of Shirin?
faq.a: Romanization variants include Shirin, shirin. Script forms are شيرين, شِيرِين, شیرین, شیریں, शीरीन.

faq.q: Is Shirin a boy's or girl's name?
faq.a: Documented usage records this form as female. Gender is not inferred from the meaning of the word, and actual use may vary between communities.
